tools.name: mcp__ccd_turn__wrap_up
tools.description:
Fill the "next step" box the app shows at the end of your turn: a two-or-three-sentence recap and, when this turn leaves the user a decision to make or a step to take, one question and buttons that answer it; a turn with nothing pending ends with the recap alone, and the app then draws no box. Call it once in EVERY turn in which you kept a task list, changed files, ran commands, or completed multi-step work: when this turn's work is done, before any closing message (it also checks off the task list; no closing update_plan is needed). Skip it for short answers, pure conversation, or a brief read-and-explain turn — a reply that names a follow-up is not brief: propose it and call this.

The result says which case below applies. When the box shows your question, it ends your turn: write no text after this call, since the recap and question say what the user needs and your work above holds the detail. Otherwise your closing message is ordinary text right after this call, the last thing you say this turn: your answer to the user in full, with any question the box did not show.

Fields — recap and ask are said to the user, in the second person; a reply button's label and message are the user's words back to you:
- recap: what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified (for example: nothing committed, or not checked in the app). Two or three short sentences, about 40 words / 300 characters, in the project's own words. No recommendation here.
- ask (with actions, only when the next move is the user's call — a choice of approach, a go-ahead to commit, push, post or send, an approval): just that ONE decision in one short sentence, never two joined by "and" ("Which fix first?"), with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give: your pick, actions[0], is drawn as the primary button. At most 100 characters.
Every field is a top-level parameter holding plain prose (actions: a JSON array); none contains markup or another field.

recap.description: Two or three short sentences to the user (≤300 chars): what is now true or changed, then where it stands, including what is not done or not verified. Its first sentence is the sidebar status.

ask.description: The one question (≤100 chars) when the next move is the user's call — a choice, a go-ahead, an approval: the decision alone, with no reason or recommendation and without listing the options the buttons give (actions[0] is your pick). Omit it, and actions, when nothing waits on the user.

blocked.description: true when your work stops here until the user answers (the app marks the session as waiting on them); omit when the answer can wait.

action.description: An app action update_plan's result listed as available now, or one your own work this turn made available; anything else is refused, and one that stops being available later is dropped (as actions[0], with your ask and the other answers), so do not guess. Omit for a reply.

label.description: For a reply: the button text, 1–3 words (4 only when three cannot say it) / 24 characters — "Yes, fix 1", "Fix 2 instead", "Not now": a button, not a sentence; the detail goes in message. No "@", no leading / or !. Ignored for an app action (the app's own label is used).

message.description: For a reply: what the click sends, up to 300 characters of plain text — no "@" anywhere, no leading / or !. Omit when the label is the whole message.

actions.description: 1–2 buttons, recommendation first. They are answers to your ask: the first accepts your recommendation, and another is there only when it is a realistic alternative the user might pick instead — not a menu of everything you mentioned. When blocked is true, they are the most likely answers to your question. While Auto-fix is on for the session's PR, none offers to watch it, fix CI, resolve conflicts or address comments.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__browser_batch
tools.description: Execute a sequence of Browser pane tool calls in ONE round trip. Each item is {name, input} where input is exactly what you'd pass to that tool standalone. Actions execute SEQUENTIALLY (not in parallel) and stop on the first error. Use this tool extensively to quickly execute work whenever you can predict two or more steps ahead — e.g. navigate, click a field, type, press Return, screenshot. Each tool's own permission check runs per item — a step on a site the user hasn't allowed either asks the user inline (and continues if they allow) or is refused, which stops the batch; if a step is refused for a missing permission, call that tool on its own (that call can ask the user), then batch the rest. Screenshots and other images are returned interleaved with outputs; coordinates you write in THIS batch refer to the screenshot taken BEFORE this call. browser_batch cannot be nested, and preview_start is not batchable — but if the Browser pane isn't open yet, a batch whose FIRST action is navigate with a url opens it (other actions still need an open page).

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
tools.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Code_iOS_Simulator__control
schema.description: Run, test, and visually verify iOS apps in the iOS Simulator on this Mac. Use this whenever the user wants to see or try their iOS app — "run my app", "test this on iPhone", "does this look right?", "try the new screen" — not only when they mention the simulator by name. Simulator only: this tool cannot drive or stream a physical iPhone or iPad. If the user wants the app on their real device ("on my iPhone", "on my device"), build and deploy for the device with your normal build tools instead, and say the live panel only shows simulators. 'attach' opens a live panel so the user can watch — when the user wants to see the app, call 'attach' FIRST, before building: it is cheap, opens instantly on a booted simulator, and errors harmlessly when nothing is booted (boot or build, then retry it). 'launch' installs and launches a built .app — build it first, with the user's own build tooling or this server's 'build' tool when this session has it; launch re-attaches on its own, but do not rely on that instead of the early attach. Screenshots and tap/swipe/text verification are headless and need no panel. Don't open the panel when the user only asked to build/compile or to run unit tests. Coordinates are in device points (origin top-left); the 'launch' result reports the device's point dimensions.

action.description: What to do. 'attach' opens the live simulator panel for the user — call it BEFORE you build or launch, as soon as the user wants to see the app: on a booted simulator it opens immediately, and otherwise it returns a clear, harmless error (boot or build first, then retry it). Do not skip the early attach because 'launch' also attaches — the panel should be open before the build starts. The panel is the user's view, not a precondition — 'screenshot' and input actions work without it. Skip it only when the user has no interest in watching; 'launch' installs and launches an .app (it also re-attaches, but call 'attach' early rather than relying on that); 'screenshot' returns a PNG of the current screen; 'tap'/'swipe'/'text'/'button' inject input; 'touch_path' performs a single-finger drag along an arbitrary path (eased curves, long-press-then-drag); 'touch2_path' is the two-finger variant for pinch/rotate; 'open_url' opens a deep link; 'detach' closes the panel/stream. NOTE: a 'swipe' or 'touch_path' whose start point is on-screen and within 4pt of an edge performs the OS edge gesture instead of a plain drag — left=back, top=notification shade, bottom=home/app-switcher, right=Control Center (mapped to the current interface orientation). Start more than 4pt from the edge to drag or scroll content near the bezel.

## claude-in-chrome
**IMPORTANT: If the Chrome browser tools are deferred (must be loaded via ToolSearch before use), load them with ToolSearch before calling them, and batch every tool you expect to need into ONE ToolSearch call (the select query accepts a comma-separated list). Do NOT load tools one at a time; each separate ToolSearch call wastes a full round-trip.**

Start a browser task whose tools are not yet loaded with a single call loading the core set:

ToolSearch with query "select:mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_context_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__navigate,mcp__claude-in-chrome__computer,mcp__claude-in-chrome__read_page,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_create_mcp,mcp__claude-in-chrome__tabs_close_mcp"

Add task-specific tools to the same call when the task obviously needs them: read_console_messages / read_network_requests for debugging, form_input for forms, gif_creator for recordings, javascript_tool for page scripting. Only issue a second ToolSearch if the task later needs a tool you did not anticipate.

## computer-use
You have a computer-use MCP available (tools named `mcp__computer-use__*`). It lets you take screenshots of the user's desktop and control it with mouse clicks, keyboard input, and scrolling.

**Pick the right tool for the app.** Each tier trades speed/precision against coverage:

1. **Dedicated MCP for the app** — if the task is in an app that has its own MCP (Slack, Gmail, Calendar, Linear, etc.) and that MCP is connected, use it. API-backed tools are fast and precise.
2. **Chrome MCP** (`mcp__claude-in-chrome__*`) — if the target is a web app and there's no dedicated MCP for it, use the browser tools. DOM-aware, much faster than clicking pixels. If the Chrome extension isn't connected, ask the user to install it rather than falling through to computer use.
3. **Computer use** — for native desktop apps (Maps, Notes, Finder, Photos, System Settings, any third-party native app) and cross-app workflows. Computer use IS the right tool here — don't decline a native-app task just because there's no dedicated MCP for it.

This is about what's available, not error handling — if a dedicated MCP tool errors, debug or report it rather than silently retrying via a slower tier.

**Look before you assert.** If the user asks about app state (what's open, what's connected, what an app can do), take a screenshot and check before answering. Don't answer from memory — the user's setup or app version may differ from what you expect. If you're about to say an app doesn't support an action, that claim should be grounded in what you just saw on screen, not general knowledge. Similarly, `list_granted_applications` or a fresh `screenshot` is cheaper than a wrong assertion about what's running.

**Loading via ToolSearch — load in bulk, not one-by-one:** if computer-use tools are in the deferred list, load them ALL in a single ToolSearch call: `{ query: "computer-use", max_results: 30 }`. The keyword search matches the server-name substring in every tool name, so one query returns the entire toolkit. Don't use `select:` for individual tools — that's one round-trip per tool.

**Access flow:** before any computer-use action you must call `request_access` with the list of applications you need. The user approves each application explicitly, and you may need to call it again mid-task if you discover you need another application. Finder is an application like any other: clicking the desktop, the Dock, or a Finder window (including Go to Folder) requires a Finder grant. The menu bar does not, as long as the app that is frontmost is one you already have access to.

**Tiered apps:** some apps are granted at a restricted tier based on their category — the tier is displayed in the approval dialog and returned in the `request_access` response:

184	+                 and (g.home_id in (select cfbd_id from fbs_teams f where f.season = g.season)
185	+                      or g.away_id in (select cfbd_id from fbs_teams f where f.season = g.season))),
186	+           p as (select distinct season_type, week from plays where season = ?),

188	+           select done.season_type, done.week from done

379	+        return (f'<svg class="strip" data-series="{row["name"]}" width="{width}" height="{height}" '

381	+    lo, hi = min(vals), max(vals)
382	+    span = (hi - lo) or 1.0
383	+    lo, hi = lo - 0.1 * span, hi + 0.1 * span
384	+    span = hi - lo
385	+    pad = 8
386	+
387	+    def x(v: float) -> float:

389	+        return round(pad + frac * (width - 2 * pad), 1)
390	+
391	+    xa, xe = x(row["cut_average"]), x(row["cut_elite"])

397	+             f'<line data-label="cut_average" x1="{xa}" y1="{mid - 6}" x2="{xa}" y2="{mid + 6}" class="cut"/>',
398	+             f'<line data-label="cut_elite" x1="{xe}" y1="{mid - 6}" x2="{xe}" y2="{mid + 6}" class="cut"/>']
399	+    if row.get("cfp_median") is not None:

404	+        parts.append(f'<circle data-label="value" cx="{x(row["value"])}" cy="{mid}" r="4.5" class="{cls}"/>')

457	+"""Parquet snapshot of every table, the way machines exchange this DB (the DB itself never travels).
458	+
459	+Files are written to a local temp folder, then copied into the target folder, then the manifest is written last, so
460	+a reader never sees a manifest that promises files not yet there. A snapshot never shrinks without --force: if the
461	+published manifest records more rows for any table than the DB holds, the DB is probably an older copy."""
462	+from __future__ import annotations
463	+
464	+import json
465	+import shutil
466	+import tempfile
467	+from datetime import datetime
468	+from pathlib import Path
469	+
470	+import duckdb
471	+
472	+MANIFEST = "manifest.json"
473	+
474	+
475	+class SnapshotRefused(Exception):
476	+    def __init__(self, shrinking: dict[str, tuple[int, int]]):
477	+        self.shrinking = shrinking
478	+        detail = ", ".join(f"{t} {pub} published, {db} in the DB" for t, (pub, db) in sorted(shrinking.items()))
479	+        super().__init__(f"snapshot would shrink: {detail}. Pass --force-snapshot if the DB is right.")
480	+
481	+
482	+def export_snapshot(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, out_dir: Path, exported_at: datetime, force: bool = False) -> dict[str, int]:
483	+    out_dir = Path(out_dir)
484	+    tables = sorted(r[0] for r in con.execute("show tables").fetchall())
485	+    rows = {t: con.execute(f'select count(*) from "{t}"').fetchone()[0] for t in tables}
486	+    manifest = out_dir / MANIFEST
487	+    if manifest.exists() and not force:
488	+        published = json.loads(manifest.read_text()).get("rows", {})
489	+        shrinking = {t: (int(published[t]), rows.get(t, 0)) for t in published if int(published[t]) > rows.get(t, 0)}
490	+        if shrinking:
491	+            raise SnapshotRefused(shrinking)
492	+    out_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
493	+    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
494	+        for t in tables:
495	+            local = Path(tmp) / f"{t}.parquet"
496	+            con.execute(f"copy \"{t}\" to '{local}' (format parquet)")
497	+            shutil.copy2(local, out_dir / local.name)
498	+    manifest.write_text(json.dumps({"exported_at": exported_at.isoformat(), "rows": rows}, indent=2))
499	+    return rows

"""Iterative opponent adjustment of team-game quantities.

For quantity q with league mean L: q_for_adj = q_for - (D_opp - L), q_against_adj = q_against - (O_opp - L),
where O_t and D_t are each team's mean adjusted for and against values, recomputed every iteration.
FBS-vs-FBS rows only; FCS rows keep their raw values and are flagged by is_fcs_opponent."""
from __future__ import annotations

from datetime import datetime

import duckdb
import pandas as pd

from cfb_benchmarks.config import Config
from cfb_benchmarks.db import QUANTITIES


def adjust_frame(df: pd.DataFrame, quantity: str, iterations: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Pure core. Columns needed: cfbd_id, opponent_id, <q>_for, <q>_against. Adds <q>_for_adj, <q>_against_adj."""
    f, a = f"{quantity}_for", f"{quantity}_against"
    out = df.copy()
    out[f"{f}_adj"] = pd.NA
    out[f"{a}_adj"] = pd.NA
    valid_for = out[f].notna()
    valid_against = out[a].notna()
    if not valid_for.any() and not valid_against.any():
        return out
    league = pd.concat([out.loc[valid_for, f], out.loc[valid_against, a]]).astype(float).mean()
    for_adj = out[f].astype(float).copy()
    against_adj = out[a].astype(float).copy()
    for _ in range(iterations):
        off_rating = for_adj[valid_for].groupby(out.loc[valid_for, "cfbd_id"]).mean()
        def_rating = against_adj[valid_against].groupby(out.loc[valid_against, "cfbd_id"]).mean()
        opp_def = out["opponent_id"].map(def_rating).fillna(league)
        opp_off = out["opponent_id"].map(off_rating).fillna(league)
        for_adj = out[f].astype(float) - (opp_def - league)
        against_adj = out[a].astype(float) - (opp_off - league)
    out.loc[valid_for, f"{f}_adj"] = for_adj[valid_for]
    out.loc[valid_against, f"{a}_adj"] = against_adj[valid_against]
    return out


def adjust_team_game_metrics(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, config: Config, built_at: datetime,
                             seasons: list[int] | None = None) -> int:
    total = 0
    for season in seasons or config.seasons():
        cols = ["cfbd_id", "game_id", "opponent_id", "is_fcs_opponent"] + [f"{q}_{s}" for q in QUANTITIES for s in ("for", "against")]
        df = con.execute(f"select {', '.join(cols)} from team_game_metrics where season = ?", [season]).df()
        if df.empty:
            continue
        fbs = df[~df["is_fcs_opponent"].fillna(False).astype(bool)].copy()
        fcs = df[df["is_fcs_opponent"].fillna(False).astype(bool)].copy()
        for q in QUANTITIES:
            fbs = adjust_frame(fbs, q, config.metrics.adjustment_iterations)
            fcs[f"{q}_for_adj"] = fcs[f"{q}_for"]
            fcs[f"{q}_against_adj"] = fcs[f"{q}_against"]
        both = pd.concat([fbs, fcs], ignore_index=True)
        adj_cols = [f"{q}_{s}_adj" for q in QUANTITIES for s in ("for", "against")]
        set_clause = ", ".join(f"{c} = ?" for c in adj_cols)
        rows = []
        for _, r in both.iterrows():
            vals = [None if pd.isna(r[c]) else float(r[c]) for c in adj_cols]
            rows.append((*vals, built_at, int(r["cfbd_id"]), int(r["game_id"])))
        con.executemany(f"update team_game_metrics set {set_clause}, built_at = ? where cfbd_id = ? and game_id = ?", rows)
        total += len(rows)
    return total

Eight metric families, eleven series once success rate, explosiveness and finishing drives
are split by side. The staff page shows all eleven. The composite and the wins model use
the eleven series; "eight" in this document refers to the families a coach sees.

**Sources (Phase 1 addendum).** EPA is CFBD's `ppa`. Finishing drives and field position come from `/drives` (start and end yards to goal, start and end offense score), not from plays. Drive-based quantities do not apply the garbage-time rule in Phase 1. A play type CFBD returns that no config list names stops the run; `config/metrics.yaml` lists every known type in exactly one list.

**Opponent adjustment.** Each team-game value is adjusted by the opponent's season mean on
the mirror metric, iterated to convergence across the season (ridge-style, the standard
approach). Raw values are kept beside adjusted ones so the adjustment is always auditable.

**Filters, stated once in config.**
- Garbage time excluded. Starting rule: margin above 38 in the 2nd quarter, 28 in the 3rd,
  22 in the 4th. Phase 1 confirms or replaces this from the literature.
- FCS opponents excluded from reference distributions and from opponent adjustment. Baylor's
  FCS games are still scored on the coach page and flagged.
- Conference title games and CFP games included in the reference. They define the cohorts.

**Cohort labels** are facts, not judgments, all from CFBD games and rankings:
made the CFP, conference champion, played in the conference title game, final AP Top 25,

from cfb_benchmarks.config import Config
from cfb_benchmarks.db import QUANTITIES, metric_columns

# One row per (team, game) for every game with at least one FBS team from `fbs_teams` and every game of a
# population team. offense-side aggregates are computed once per (game, offense) and joined twice.
PERSPECTIVES_SQL = """
with sides as (
    select game_id, season, week, season_type, is_conf_title_game, is_cfp_game,
           home_id as team_id, away_id as opp_id, away_classification as opp_class from games
    where home_points is not null and away_points is not null
    union all
    select game_id, season, week, season_type, is_conf_title_game, is_cfp_game,
           away_id as team_id, home_id as opp_id, home_classification as opp_class from games
    where home_points is not null and away_points is not null
)
select s.*,
       -- the single switch: an opponent outside that season's FBS list is FCS, whatever `games` says about classification
       (s.opp_id is null or s.opp_id not in (select cfbd_id from fbs_teams f where f.season = s.season)) as is_fcs_opponent
from sides s
where s.season = ?
  and s.team_id is not null
  and (s.team_id in (select cfbd_id from fbs_teams where season = s.season)
       or s.team_id in (select cfbd_id from teams))
"""

# A play's offense_id is NULL when the offence is an FCS team; the other side is always resolved, so the game
# row says who the offence was.
OFFENSE_SQL = """
select game_id, off_id as offense_id,
       count(*) filter (where is_offensive_play) as plays,
       avg(ppa) filter (where is_offensive_play and ppa is not null) as epa_play,
       (count(*) filter (where is_offensive_play and is_success))::double
         / nullif(count(*) filter (where is_offensive_play), 0) as success_rate,
       (count(*) filter (where is_offensive_play and not is_turnover and yards_gained >= ?))::double
         / nullif(count(*) filter (where is_offensive_play), 0) as explosiveness,
       (count(*) filter (where is_offensive_play and is_turnover))::double as turnovers,
       (count(*) filter (where is_offensive_play and (is_tfl or is_forced_fumble or is_interception or is_pass_defensed)))::double
         / nullif(count(*) filter (where is_offensive_play), 0) as havoc
from (select p.*, coalesce(p.offense_id, case when p.defense_id = g.home_id then g.away_id else g.home_id end) as off_id
      from plays p join games g on g.game_id = p.game_id) x
where season = ? and not is_garbage
group by game_id, off_id
"""

DRIVES_SQL = """
with trips as (
    select d.drive_id, d.game_id,
           coalesce(d.offense_id, case when d.defense_id = g.home_id then g.away_id else g.home_id end) as offense_id,
           d.start_yards_to_goal, d.start_offense_score, d.end_offense_score,
           (d.end_yards_to_goal <= ? or exists (
                select 1 from plays p where p.drive_id = d.drive_id and p.yards_to_goal <= ?)) as inside
    from drives d join games g on g.game_id = d.game_id where d.season = ?
)
select game_id, offense_id,
       avg(100 - start_yards_to_goal) as start_yardline,
       sum(greatest(end_offense_score - start_offense_score, 0)) filter (where inside)::double
         / nullif(count(*) filter (where inside), 0) as finishing_drives
from trips
group by game_id, offense_id
"""


def build_team_game_metrics(con: duckdb.DuckDBPyConnection, config: Config, built_at: datetime,
                            seasons: list[int] | None = None) -> int:
    yl = config.metrics.finishing_yardline
    total = 0
    for season in seasons or config.seasons():
        persp = con.execute(PERSPECTIVES_SQL, [season]).fetchall()
        off = {(g, o): r for g, o, *r in con.execute(OFFENSE_SQL, [config.metrics.explosive_yards, season]).fetchall()}
        drv = {(g, o): r for g, o, *r in con.execute(DRIVES_SQL, [yl, yl, season]).fetchall()}
        rows = []
        for game_id, s, week, stype, title, cfp, team, opp, _oc, fcs in persp:
            mine, theirs = off.get((game_id, team)), off.get((game_id, opp))
            dm, dt = drv.get((game_id, team)), drv.get((game_id, opp))
            q_for = _quantities(mine, dm)
            q_against = _quantities(theirs, dt)
            metrics = [q_for[q] for q in QUANTITIES] + [q_against[q] for q in QUANTITIES] + [None] * (2 * len(QUANTITIES))
            rows.append((team, game_id, s, week, stype, opp, fcs, title, cfp,
                         (mine[0] if mine else 0), (theirs[0] if theirs else 0), *metrics, "CFBD", built_at))
        cols = ["cfbd_id", "game_id", "season", "week", "season_type", "opponent_id", "is_fcs_opponent",
                "is_conf_title_game", "is_cfp_game", "plays_for", "plays_against", *metric_columns(), "source_system", "built_at"]
        con.executemany(
            f"insert or replace into team_game_metrics ({', '.join(cols)}) values ({', '.join('?' * len(cols))})", rows
        )
        total += len(rows)
    return total


def _quantities(off_row, drive_row) -> dict[str, float | None]:
    plays, epa, success, explosive, turnovers, havoc = off_row if off_row else (0, None, None, None, None, None)
    start_yl, finishing = drive_row if drive_row else (None, None)

import pytest

from cfb_benchmarks.ingest_plays import CoverageError
from cfb_benchmarks.live_pull import build_live_season, estimate_live_calls, missing_weeks, pull_week
from tests.conftest import LIVE, NOW, live_fake_client


def test_missing_weeks_lists_completed_weeks_without_plays_or_drives(live_db):
    assert missing_weeks(live_db, LIVE) == [("regular", 2), ("regular", 3)]


def test_pull_stops_at_the_failing_week_and_resumes_there(live_db, live_cfg):
    client = live_fake_client()
    plays, drives = pull_week(live_db, client, live_cfg, LIVE, "regular", 2, NOW)
    assert plays > 0 and drives > 0
    with pytest.raises(CoverageError):
        pull_week(live_db, client, live_cfg, LIVE, "regular", 3, NOW)        # score posted, plays not yet
    assert missing_weeks(live_db, LIVE) == [("regular", 3)]
    assert live_db.execute("select count(*) from plays where week = 3").fetchone()[0] == 0


def test_estimate_live_calls():
    assert estimate_live_calls(0) == 3 and estimate_live_calls(4) == 11


def test_build_live_season_leaves_the_reference_alone(live_db, live_cfg):
    before = live_db.execute("select count(*) from thresholds").fetchone()[0]
    counts = build_live_season(live_db, live_cfg, NOW, LIVE)
    assert counts["team_game_metrics"] > 0 and counts["team_season_metrics"] > 0
    assert live_db.execute("select count(*) from thresholds").fetchone()[0] == before
    assert live_db.execute("select count(*) from cohorts where season = ?", [LIVE]).fetchone()[0] == 0
